item.title: Distillery Country Music Series: Coty Robinson — Sat Aug 1, 1:00 PM — Trinity Stage
item.description:
A big man with a big voice. This is Coty Robinson and he is aiming to be a household name. With the loss of his mother at a young age, Robinson dived headfirst into music as a way to cope with the pain and heartbreak. For Coty, connecting with music was a way to express his own experiences, struggles, and emotions and to honour his mother's memory. Johnny Cash, Eric Church, Lee Brice, and Luke Combs have all influenced Coty’s sound and songwriting. Being a fan of country music first, Coty’s biggest aspiration is to bring the joy of connecting with fans through music, and song, and being able to share the experience with others, at any level possible. Coty lives to perform. His live show is electrifying and wins over new fans immediately through his heartfelt human connection.
Source: Distillery District

item.title: Distillery Country Music Series: Jade Hilton — Sat Aug 1, 5:00 PM — Trinity Stage
item.description:
Fast-rising country singer-songwriter Jade Hilton is making waves with her new single “I Want a Cowboy”. Written by Hilton at her parents’ farm in Norfolk County, Ontario, Hilton later brought the track south to Alabama, where it was recorded live off the floor. “I Want a Cowboy” blends Hilton’s classic country influences with a modern edge and offers an early glimpse into the music she is preparing for her upcoming album. Last year, Hilton’s breakout single “Dive Bar” earned her national attention including CTV’s Etalk, who called Hilton “the hottest new talent in country music”. Since then, Hilton has delivered standout performances at Country Music Week and Folk Music Week. She was also named a finalist for the 2025 Boots and Hearts Emerging Artist Showcase. Just last month, she headlined The Rivoli in Toronto for the first time and sold out the venue.
Source: Distillery District

item.title: Branch Art Exhibit: Works by Farzana Islam — Sun Aug 2, 12:00 AM — Albion
item.description: Throughout the month of August, the works of artist Farzana Island are on display at Albion Branch. Farzana Islam is a Bangladeshi Canadian artist and illustrator based in Toronto. She tells stories that don’t always get the spotlight, aiming to leave a feeling that stays with people. From making webcomics as a teen and tattoo apprenticeships to studying illustration at Sheridan College, she now works across illustration, animation, and 3D, bringing untold perspectives to life in human, meaningful ways. "Farzana’s work is rooted in her experience of entering the Canadian school system as an immigrant child, carrying languages and stories that didn’t always fit. Shaped by Scarborough’s vibrant diversity, her art brings to light how young people carve out belonging within educational and cultural landscapes. Through her work with youth and her lens as a queer Muslim artist, she explores identity, literacy, and amplifies voices often overlooked but quietly shared across communities." The

item.title: Town of York Historical Society - Simcoe Day in Toronto 2026 — Mon Aug 3, 1:00 PM — St. Matthew’s Clubhouse
item.description:
Celebrate Simcoe Day 2026 with Toronto history authors, booksellers, podcasters, and historical societies on Monday, August 3, 2026! For a third straight year, the York Pioneer & Historical Society (YPHS), Toronto’s First Post Office (TYHS), and the Riverdale Historical Society are partnering to bring together people who share a passion for Toronto’s rich past. Join us from 1:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. at St. Matthew’s Clubhouse, 450 Broadview Avenue (just north of Gerrard Street East) for an afternoon dedicated to exploring Toronto history! Browse curated artifact displays, meet and chat with local authors and podcasters, connect with historical societies, and take part in guided neighbourhood walks. Whether you’re a lifelong history enthusiast or simply curious about Toronto’s past, you’ll discover something new and meet others who share your interest! Admission is free. Please Note: Some book purchases will be cash only.
Source: Ontario Historical Society

item.title: 2026 Toronto History Lecture: A Grocery Store, a Library, and the Struggle for Space: ﻿Black Community-Building in Toronto, 1920s–1960 — Tue Aug 4, 7:30 PM — online
item.description: The 15th annual Toronto History Lecture will be held online via Zoom on Tuesday, August 4, at 7:30 pm EDT. We hope you will join us! The event is free to attend, but you must register. (It will be recorded, so if your schedule or time zone doesn’t accommodate 7:30, you can time-shift.) This year’s Toronto History Lecture tells the story of the Home Service Association, a Black community organization in Toronto whose roots trace back to 1918, emerging from wartime efforts to support Black servicemen. The organization relocated multiple times across the city after its early building was condemned, continually adapting its programs to meet community needs. By the mid-twentieth century, it operated from Bathurst Street as a vibrant community hub, offering cultural programming, a cooperative grocery store, and a library. This little-known history offers a compelling, human-scale account of how communities in Toronto built spaces of belonging, support, and collective life. Our 2026 speak
